requirements.name: E-UTRAN / MBMS-dedicated cells

cases.case: CAS every 40 ms at 15 kHz, rt-mbms-tx
cases.what: The cell acquisition subframe (non-MBSFN, 15 kHz, configured cyclic prefix) with MIB and PCFICH recurs every 40 ms, but PSS/SSS are written whenever the raw TTI is divisible by 4 in subframe 0, that is in every second radio frame, so also in subframe 0 of frames that are otherwise MBSFN-typed, in rt-mbms-tx.

cases.case: CAS every 40 ms at 15 kHz, rt-mbms-tx-for-qrd-and-crd
cases.what: The variant for QRD and CRD is a regular LTE cell with no MBMS-dedicated mode: PSS/SSS are put in subframes 0 and 5 of every radio frame and the PBCH and PCFICH in subframe 0 of every radio frame, so there is no cell acquisition subframe every 40 ms.

cases.case: Normal or extended cyclic prefix
cases.what: In both repositories the cell cyclic prefix is normal or extended by the extended_cp setting.

noted: PSS/SSS are placed when tti % 4 == 0 in subframe 0, which is every second radio frame, while the MIB and PCFICH follow SFN % 4 == 0.

requirements.name: Deployment models (informative) / Deployment with self-contained 5G Broadcast Transmitter

cases.case: eNodeB integrated with core functions
cases.what: Both repositories run the eNodeB together with srsepc (MME, HSS, SPGW) and a basic MBMS gateway on one host as separate processes, but there is no BM-SC and no xMB interface; the externally visible interfaces are Uu, SGi-mb and M1-U, not xMB and Uu only.

requirements.name: Transmitter requirements for LTE-based 5G / Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC)

cases.case: BM-SC function in the transmitter
cases.what: Neither repository contains a BM-SC function; the BM-SC is a separate project.

cases.case: EPS MBMS procedures of the BM-SC
cases.what: The transmitter has no BM-SC procedures (no session start, update or stop signalling from a BM-SC); MBMS control data comes from configuration files.

requirements.name: Transmitter requirements for LTE-based 5G / MBMS GW

cases.case: MBMS GW function in the transmitter
cases.what: Each repository includes a basic MBMS gateway in srsepc that reads IP packets from a virtual sgi_mb interface and sends them as GTP-U with a fixed TEID 0xAAAA (IPv4 only) to an M1-U multicast address; it has no Sm interface, no session start or stop and no MBMS bearer context, so only a subset of the TS 23.246 MBMS-GW functions exists.

noted: Basic gateway only: GTPv2-C Sm session control is not implemented in either transmitter repository (the standalone rt-mbms-gw has it).

requirements.name: E-UTRAN / General

cases.case: eNodeB function in the transmitter
cases.what: Both repositories are srsRAN-based eNodeBs with MBMS (MBSFN, PMCH, MCCH, SIB13) support; the individual clause 6.4 functions are judged in their own statements.

requirements.name: E-UTRAN / MBMS-dedicated cells

cases.case: MBMS-dedicated cells only
cases.what: rt-mbms-tx can run as an FeMBMS dedicated cell (option off by default, on in the sample configuration) but also as an MBMS/unicast mixed cell; the qrd repository has no dedicated-cell mode and serves MBSFN subframes in a mixed cell.

requirements.name: E-UTRAN / MBMS transmission

cases.case: MBMS transmission per 36.300 15.3.3
cases.what: Both eNodeBs transmit MBMS as MBSFN on the PMCH with an MTCH over RLC UM from the multicast M1-U input; only a single MCH can be transmitted.

cases.case: MCCH configuration and scheduling without counting
cases.what: SIB13 MCCH parameters are parsed from the configuration and used by the PHY and MAC to schedule the MCCH, and counting is not implemented as the clause allows, but the MBSFNAreaConfiguration content is hard-coded (one PMCH, TMGI service id 0 with PLMN 00003, fixed rf64 periods and allocation; only the data MCS comes from configuration).

requirements.name: E-UTRAN / Physical channels and signals

cases.case: Downlink physical channels only
cases.what: Both eNodeBs keep the unicast srsRAN uplink chain (PUSCH and PUCCH decoding, PRACH) in addition to the downlink channels; the qrd variant only removes the need for uplink connectivity to deliver MBMS.

cases.case: PMCH supported
cases.what: Both eNodeBs encode the PMCH for MBSFN subframes.

cases.case: PDSCH supported
cases.what: Both eNodeBs encode the PDSCH (used for system information).

cases.case: Only the following physical channels are supported according to [16]:
cases.what: Besides the downlink broadcast channels the transmitter still contains the unicast uplink receivers (PUSCH, PUCCH, PRACH) of the srsRAN eNB, so it does not support only the listed channels.

requirements.name: E-UTRAN / RLC layer

cases.case: BCCH in RLC transparent mode
cases.what: System information PDUs go from RRC straight to the MAC and the PDSCH without RLC headers or segmentation, which is transparent mode behaviour.

cases.case: MTCH and MCCH in RLC UM
cases.what: MTCH bearers are created as RLC UM entities and the MCCH payload is built with a one-byte RLC UM header.

cases.case: RLC operation for MTCH and MCCH per 36.300 15.3.3
cases.what: The MBMS logical channels use RLC UM as for MBSFN transmission.

requirements.name: Functional Elements for the Evolved Packet System / MBMS Control plane function

cases.case: MBMS control plane function in the MME
cases.what: The srsepc MME has no MBMS control plane (no Sm or M3 interface); the eNodeB takes MBMS control data from configuration files.

cases.case: MME filtering of session control towards MCEs
cases.what: There is no MCE and no M3 interface, so no filtering by MBMS service area.

requirements.name: Functional Elements for the Evolved Packet System / E-UTRAN

cases.case: E-UTRAN receives IP multicast
cases.what: The eNodeB joins the configured IP multicast group on M1-U and receives the GTP-U encapsulated MBMS payload.

noted: The join is any-source (IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP), not source-specific.

cases.what: No QCI mapping to radio configuration per MBMS UE category exists.

cases.what: The eNodeB does not schedule point-to-point traffic on unused MBMS resources; MBSFN subframes carry only MCCH and MTCH data.

cases.what: No MooD support (no popularity based switching between unicast and MBMS).

cases.what: No shared MBMS network function exists; each transmitter serves one configured service area.

cases.case: RAN node dedicated to MBMS
cases.what: The transmitter can be deployed as an MBMS dedicated RAN node (FeMBMS dedicated cell in rt-mbms-tx).

cases.case: Shared MME function
cases.what: Condition not met for the shared MME: srsepc has a single MME with no shared-network (multi-operator) function.

cases.case: Beamformed CSI-RS (CLASS B)
cases.what: No CSI-RS beamforming or CLASS B eMIMO-Type is transmitted.

cases.case: - Non-precoded CSI-RS operation is supported by CLASS A eMIMO-Type with one CSI-RS ...
cases.what: No CSI-RS transmission or eMIMO class A configuration exists.

cases.case: Transmit diversity, specifically space frequency block coding (SFBC), is supported if ...
cases.what: The eNB has no NB-IoT operation, so the condition is never met.

cases.case: - Non-code-book-based pre-coding with or without pre-coding feedback.
cases.what: Only transmission modes 1 to 4 (codebook or diversity) exist; no DMRS-based non-codebook precoding.

cases.case: For slot/subslot based transmission, multi-antenna transmission with up to 4 transmit ...
cases.what: There is no slot or subslot based transmission.

cases.case: Multi-antenna transmission with up to 8 transmit antennas is supported.
cases.what: The transmitters support at most 4 antenna ports (SRSRAN_MAX_PORTS 4) and transmission modes 1 to 4, with 2 ports for modes above 1, and MBMS is sent on one port; 8 transmit antennas are not supported.

requirements.name: MBMS / Service Continuity

cases.case: UE priority for MBMS versus unicast near a CSG cell
cases.what: No handling of proximity indication to a CSG cell or of MBMS interest priority exists in the RRC.

requirements.name: Introduction / General

cases.case: MCCH carrying MBMSCountingRequest
cases.what: The eNodeB never builds an MBMSCountingRequest; the MCCH carries only MBSFNAreaConfiguration.

cases.case: MCE inside the eNodeB
cases.what: The eNodeB has no MCE function and no M2 interface; the MCCH content is built from configuration files.

requirements.name: Deployment models (informative) / Deployment with separated Core and RAN functions

cases.case: MBMS GW, MME and BM-SC in one device
cases.what: The standalone gateway is a separate process with no MME or BM-SC inside; the transmitter repositories bundle a basic gateway with an MME and the eNodeB but no BM-SC.

requirements.name: Functional Elements for the Evolved Packet System / MBMS GW

cases.case: One or more MBMS GW entities
cases.what: The gateway is a standalone process configured per instance (own egress interface, multicast group and MME peers), so several can be run in one PLMN.

cases.case: MBMS GW stand-alone or co-located
cases.what: rt-mbms-gw builds as a stand-alone binary; rt-mbms-tx also ships a basic gateway process next to the eNodeB and MME of the same product.

cases.case: UTRAN multicast address allocation and RNC join
cases.what: The gateway serves E-UTRAN only (M1-U to eNodeBs); there is no UTRAN, Iu or SGSN interface.

cases.case: Fall back to point to point for UTRAN
cases.what: The gateway has no UTRAN support and no point-to-point fall-back.

cases.case: - In the case of E-UTRAN access, and if the MBMS-GW supports both IPv4 and IPv6, it ...
cases.what: The gateway uses a single IPv4 multicast distribution address that is configured or supplied through the control interface (not allocated by the gateway); IPv6 is rejected and there is no dual-stack allocation.

cases.case: NOTE 3: Care should be taken to avoid clashes among C-TEIDs generated in MBMS-GWs. and ...
cases.what: The C-TEID comes from configuration (default 0xAAAA per session, hard-coded 0xAAAA in the basic srsepc gateway); nothing allocates unique C-TEIDs or checks for clashes with other MBMS-GWs or the RAN.

requirements.name: IP Multicast distribution / General

cases.case: IP multicast distribution enabled by configuration
cases.what: Distribution of the MBMS payload towards the eNodeBs on an IP multicast group (address, egress interface and TTL) is set in the configuration of both gateways.

cases.case: Source Specific Multicast model
cases.what: The gateway signals the multicast source address to the MME when one is configured, but it sends M1-U to a plain group address without enforcing the SSM address range, the basic gateway in the transmitter has no source address, and the eNodeB joins the group without a source (any-source join).

noted: Multicast is the only distribution mode; it cannot be switched off.

requirements.name: IP Multicast distribution / IP Multicast distribution for E-UTRAN and UTRAN for EPS

cases.case: Multicast address reuse across bearer services
cases.what: All sessions of a gateway use the one configured M1-U multicast group, so an address is reused across bearer services; the gateway does not require unique addresses.

cases.case: MBMS GW assigns multicast addresses per RFC 4607
cases.what: The gateway does not assign multicast addresses; the distribution address is taken from the operator configuration (or control command) and is not checked against the RFC 4607 SSM range.

cases.case: Several MBMS GWs coordinated by configuration
cases.what: The multicast address of each gateway instance is set in its own configuration, so addresses of several gateways can be coordinated by configuration.

cases.case: Coordinated TEID ranges
cases.what: The C-TEID of each session is a configured value, so TEIDs can be coordinated with the eNodeB by configuration; the gateway does not manage ranges itself and the basic gateway in the transmitter uses a fixed TEID.

requirements.name: Charging requirement / Bearer level charging for MBMS

cases.case: Charging information collection
cases.what: The gateway collects no charging information.

cases.case: Charging information in the MBMS bearer context
cases.what: The session context holds no charging related information elements.

cases.case: MBMS GW as part of another element
cases.what: The gateway can be stand-alone (rt-mbms-gw) or shipped as part of the transmitter package (srsmbms in rt-mbms-tx).

cases.case: IP multicast between the MBMS GW and the eNodeBs
cases.what: Both gateways send the MBMS payload as GTP-U on an IP multicast group and the eNodeB joins that group.

cases.case: BM-SC, MME and MBMS GW in one physical entity
cases.what: The BM-SC is its own executable that drives a separate MBMS gateway over a TCP control endpoint and a UDP tunnel; it contains no MME or gateway function.

cases.case: BM-SC functions for several services from one element
cases.what: One BM-SC instance serves the ROM service announcement channel and every xMB-C service and session.

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / General

cases.case: BM-SC as entry point for content provider transmissions
cases.what: Content providers enter through the xMB-C interface (mutual TLS), and the BM-SC initiates the MBMS bearer through the gateway and delivers the content as FLUTE.

cases.case: A BM-SC for each MBMS user service
cases.what: Every service the repository announces (the ROM SACH and each xMB-C service) is handled by this BM-SC.

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / Membership Function

cases.case: Subscription data of MBMS service users
cases.what: The BM-SC has no membership function: no user subscription data, membership management or user charging records.

cases.case: Charging records for MBMS service users
cases.what: The BM-SC has no membership function: no user subscription data, membership management or user charging records.

cases.case: Membership management at user service level
cases.what: The BM-SC has no membership function: no user subscription data, membership management or user charging records.

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / Session and Transmission Function

cases.case: Schedule MBMS session transmissions
cases.what: The BM-SC publishes a start time per session in the Schedule Description fragment of the service announcement, but it starts and stops the bearer and the transmission when the content provider sets the session state, not by an internal schedule.

cases.case: Retransmissions and MBMS Session Identifier
cases.what: The BM-SC does not schedule session retransmissions and sends no MBMS Session Identifier to distinguish them.

cases.case: Transport parameter: service area
cases.what: The service area code of the session is passed to the gateway with the TMGI, C-TEID and distribution address when the bearer is started.

cases.case: Transport parameter: quality of service
cases.what: The BM-SC does not send QoS (QCI, ARP, bit rates) to the gateway; the gateway uses its own configured profile.

cases.case: Initiate and terminate MBMS bearer resources
cases.what: The BM-SC starts (START or UPDATE) and stops (STOP) the MBMS session in the gateway, which drives the Sm session, around the transmission of a session.

cases.case: Send MBMS data
cases.what: The BM-SC sends content as FLUTE (or raw UDP for transport mode) packets to the gateway tunnel, addressed to the session multicast address.

cases.case: Authenticate, authorise and accept content from external sources
cases.what: The xMB-C server requires a client certificate that verifies against the configured trusted certificate and then accepts content from the provider (pushed or pulled by URL).

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / Proxy and Transport Function

cases.case: BM-SC functions for services split over several physical elements
cases.what: All BM-SC functions run in one process; no coordination between several physical BM-SC elements exists.

cases.case: Charging records for content provider charging
cases.what: No charging records are generated for transmitted data.

cases.case: Proxy and transport as intermediate for MBMS data
cases.what: For transport-mode sessions the BM-SC relays provider datagrams, as raw UDP packets, to the gateway tunnel.

requirements.name: MBMS Content Transfer for the same MBMS User Service for GPRS and EPS / Separate MBMS Bearer Services for the same MBMS User Service

cases.case: Two multicast addresses or TMGIs for one user service
cases.what: Each session has one TMGI and one multicast address; no second address or TMGI is allocated for separate bearer services of the same user service.

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / Location Dependent Content Transfer for the same MBMS User Service (Broadcast Mode only)

cases.case: Different content in different areas
cases.what: Each session of a service carries its own TMGI, multicast address and service area code supplied by the content provider, so separate bearers can cover different areas, but the BM-SC does not share one TMGI across the sessions of a user service, allocates no Flow Identifier and does not check that the service areas of the sessions do not overlap.

cases.case: Service areas of sessions of a user service do not overlap
cases.what: The BM-SC takes the service area per session from the provider and does not check that areas of sessions of one service are disjoint.

requirements.name: Broadcast-Multicast Service Centre (BM-SC) / MBMS User Service Consumption Reporting (Broadcast mode only)

cases.case: Consumption monitoring and reporting
cases.what: Consumption reporting settings are stored with the service but the BM-SC has no reporting endpoint and no monitoring of consumption.

requirements.name: Quality-of-Service / Quality-of-Service for EPS

cases.case: UE category for QCI derivation

requirements.name: CBC Functionality

cases.case: CBC connected to several nodes
cases.what: Warnings are sent to one configured MME bridge endpoint; connections to several MMEs, RNCs, BSCs or PWS-IWFs are not supported.

cases.case: CBC connected to several CBEs
cases.what: The portal originates warnings itself as the only cell broadcast entity; it accepts no connections from other CBEs.

cases.case: Allocation of serial numbers
cases.what: The portal allocates the 16-bit Serial Number as an incrementing counter per alert type (kept in memory), not with the geographical scope, message code and update number layout of the cell broadcast serial number.

cases.case: Set of cells for a CBS message
cases.what: The operator draws warning areas that are sent as Warning-Area-Coordinates in the Write-Replace-Warning-Request; the portal does not determine a cell list itself, the MME and eNodeBs resolve the area.

cases.case: Geographical scope in the Serial Number
cases.what: The serial number carries no geographical scope indication.

cases.case: Start time of the broadcast
cases.what: The portal sends the Write-Replace-Warning-Request to the MME as soon as the operator submits the alert; no start time is determined or scheduled and the request built has no start-time field.

cases.case: End of the broadcast and stop instruction
cases.what: The operator can stop a warning at any time: the portal sends a Stop-Warning-Request with the message identifier and serial number to the MME, which relays it to the eNodeBs; the portal does not itself determine or schedule an end time and does not address each node.

cases.case: Repetition period of the broadcast
cases.what: The portal sets the repetition period (default 4096, operator adjustable) and the number of broadcasts requested in the request.

cases.case: Lists of cells towards a BSC or RNC
cases.what: Condition not met: the portal talks SBc-AP to an MME and has no BSC or RNC interface, so it works on warning areas rather than lists of cells.

cases.case: The CBC shall be responsible for the management of CBS messages including:
cases.what: The portal acts as a cell broadcast entity towards the MME: it allocates a serial number per alert type, sends Write-Replace-Warning with repetition period, broadcast count and warning area, and a Stop-Warning to cease broadcast; it does not pad pages, handle languages, choose start time per cell, determine cell sets or modify held messages, and holds no message store.
